verses.1: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted; and the train of His robe + 6:1 Or the hem of His robe filled the temple.
verses.2: Above Him stood seraphim, each having six wings: With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they were flying.
verses.4: At the sound of their voices the doorposts and thresholds shook, and the temple was filled with smoke.
verses.6: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.
verses.7:
And with it he touched my mouth and said:
 “Now that this has touched your lips,
 your iniquity is removed
 and your sin is atoned for.”
verses.8:
Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying:
 “Whom shall I send?
 Who will go for Us?”
 And I said:
 “Here am I. Send me!”
verses.9:
And He replied:
 “Go and tell this people,
 ‘Be ever hearing, but never understanding;
 be ever seeing, but never perceiving.’ + 6:9 Hebrew; LXX ‘You shall be ever hearing, but never understanding; you shall be ever seeing, but never perceiving.’ Cited in Matthew 13:14|MAT 13:14 , Mark 4:12, Luke 8:10, and Acts 28:26
verses.10:
Make the hearts of this people calloused;
 deafen their ears and close their eyes.
 Otherwise they might see with their eyes,
 hear with their ears,
 understand with their hearts,
 and turn and be healed. + 6:10 Hebrew; LXX For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them. Cited in Matthew 13:15|MAT 13:15 , Mark 4:12, John 12:40, and Acts 28:27 ”
verses.11:
Then I asked:
 “How long, O Lord?”
 And He replied:
 “Until the cities lie ruined
 and without inhabitant,
 until the houses are left unoccupied
 and the land is desolate and ravaged,
verses.12:
until the LORD has driven men far away
 and the land is utterly forsaken.
verses.13:
And though a tenth remains in the land,
 it will be burned again.
 As the terebinth and oak leave stumps when felled,
 so the holy seed will be a stump in the land.”

metadata.source: Derived from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB). Missing verses restored from the Textus Receptus tradition for completeness.
